sources.takeaway: SAM is the recommended protocol for non-Java apps; i2pd support for newer SAM 3.2/3.3 features lags, so keep DHT core transport-neutral.
I2P peer/node compact info uses Destination hashes, and secure node ID rules bind Node ID bytes to Destination hash.
I2P documents full and partial keyspace Sybil/floodfill risks; the app DHT should assume adversarial neighborhoods exist.
Ed25519, salt, seq, CAS, signature validation, value-size limit, and target derivation remain the mutable baseline.
Mutable torrents are a concrete use case for pubkey+salt subscribed mutable heads.
Disjoint paths, crypto puzzles, and sibling broadcast are core security-shaped Kademlia ideas.
Social/trust edges can inform optional bootstrap hints, but should not become global identity authority.
Sloppy hash table ideas motivate hot-key/breadcrumb placement while content stays outside the DHT.
Provider records, validators, republish/expiration intervals, quorum, and entry correction are useful vocabulary.
Region-grouped/batched reproviding is an important pattern for high-volume providers.
Semantically false provider records and early termination can enable content eclipse.
